articles.title: Battery system failures fell 98% in 7 years, but older systems need special care: report
articles.summary: The Electric Power Research Institute analysis found a dramatic drop in energy storage system failures from 2018 to 2025 amid a host of technology and project improvements. “Early-vintage” systems may require retrofits, however.

articles.title: How small batteries are helping one NYC business cut energy costs
articles.summary: Food technology platform Wonder said it is saving about 5% on energy expenses using stationary plug-in batteries. “Our No. 1 goal was to figure out how we can reduce our utility bills, shave the peaks off of our utility usage,” a senior VP for the company said.

articles.title: PG&E warns of more shutoffs as fire conditions continue threatening California grid
articles.summary: The shutoffs — potentially affecting more than two dozen counties, mostly in northern and central California — could continue through Saturday.

articles.title: Solving California’s energy affordability crisis can help the whole nation
articles.summary: The state's electricity prices are double the national average, and wildfires are a big reason — but far from the only one. Fresh leadership can show the way on regulatory, financial and operational reform, write experts at GridLab and Energy Innovation.

articles.title: FERC approves Duke large load transmission rules despite cost-shift concerns
articles.summary: Commissioner David Rosner said that Duke Energy Carolinas’ proposal offers “meaningful, if imperfect, new protections,” adding that consumer protections are “inadequate across the country” and FERC may need to take further action.

articles.title: FERC rejects most of PJM’s large load interconnection plan
articles.summary: The PJM Interconnection’s plan for curtailing large loads that don’t have matching new generation intrudes on state jurisdiction and appears to be discriminatory, the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission said.

articles.title: 160K customers without power in Southeastern US as Hurricane Isaias recovery enters third day
articles.summary: Peak outages numbered approximately 950,000. Utilities said grid modernization efforts kept more customers from losing power and sped service restoration for those who did. FPL said its underground lines performed eight times better than overhead ones.

articles.title: Hinkley Point C completes 620-metre tunnel for fish
articles.summary: A tunnel boring machine has finished digging a 620-metre tunnel which will form part of Hinkley Point C's system for returning fish to the sea.

articles.title: Moves to bolster US nuclear workforce development
articles.summary: Westinghouse and the University of South Carolina are partnering to create a multidisciplinary nuclear workforce development programme to support US fleet deployment of AP1000 plants. Meanwhile, the New York Power Authority has awarded USD10 million in funding to support nuclear workforce development programmes across the state.

articles.title: BWXT's BANR microreactor selected for Canadian project
articles.summary: BWX Technologies says that its BANR microreactor has been selected by Prodigy Clean Energy, Pabineau First Nation and Eel River Bar First Nation for a proposed project in Belledune in New Brunswick.

articles.title: Concreting milestones at Chinese Hualong One units
articles.summary: The concreting of the inner containment dome has been completed at unit 3 of the Zhangzhou nuclear power plant in China's Fujian province, while concrete pours have also been completed at units 1 and 2 of the Zhaoyuan plant in Shandong province.

articles.title: Key equipment installed in BREST-OD-300 turbine hall
articles.summary: Two separator-superheaters, each 16 metres tall and weighing 95 tonnes, have been installed in their design positions for the innovative lead-cooled BREST-OD-300 fast neutron reactor.

articles.title: Deployable Energy to test its Unity nuclear battery in DOME
articles.summary: Deployable Energy's Unity demonstration reactor has been selected by the US Department of Energy's National Reactor Innovation Center for testing inside the Demonstration of Microreactor Experiments, or DOME, testbed at the Idaho National Laboratory in 2027.

articles.title: Westinghouse teams up with Hyundai E&C for Dutch FEED studies
articles.summary: South Korea's Hyundai Engineering & Construction has been contracted by Westinghouse to carry out basic design studies for the construction of two large nuclear power plants in the Netherlands based on Westinghouse's AP1000 design.

articles.title: Slovakia buys out Czech stake in new nuclear project company
articles.summary: ČEZ has sold its 49% stake in JESS, the company formed to develop new nuclear capacity in Slovakia, for EUR189 million (USD211 million).

articles.title: China's Tianwan 7 connected to the grid
articles.summary: Tianwan Nuclear Power Plant's unit 7 has been successfully connected to the grid, China National Nuclear Corporation has announced.

articles.title: Poland begins ordering long-lead components for first AP1000
articles.summary: Polskie Elektrownie Jądrowe has commissioned Westinghouse to begin ordering long-lead items for the first unit of Poland's planned first nuclear power plant, which will comprise three AP1000 reactors.

articles.title: Hydraulic tests completed at Turkey's Akkuyu 1
articles.summary: Hydraulic tests to check the primary circuit systems and equipment at unit 1 of Turkey's Akkuyu nuclear power plant have been successfully completed, paving the way for hot functional tests to begin.

articles.title: Bangladesh's Rooppur 1 achieves criticality
articles.summary: The first unit at Bangladesh's Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant achieved criticality - a self-sustaining nuclear reaction - at 15:34 on Sunday, 11 October.

articles.title: Czech SMR environmental impact assessment submitted
articles.summary: ČEZ has submitted the Environmental Impact Assessment documentation to the Ministry of the Environment for its Rolls-Royce SMR small modular reactor project in Temelín.

articles.title: Agreement signed on second Polish nuclear power plant
articles.summary: Poland's Ministry of Energy, Polskie Elektrownie Jądrowe and Polska Grupa Energetyczna have signed an agreement defining the division of tasks and principles of cooperation in preparing the construction of the country's second nuclear power plant.

articles.title: Hot testing of Chinese SMR under way
articles.summary: Tests that simulate the temperatures and pressures which the reactor systems will be subjected to during normal operation are reportedly taking place at the ACP100 small modular reactor demonstration project, under construction at the Changjiang site on China's island province of Hainan.

articles.title: Westinghouse places initial orders for Polish plant
articles.summary: Westinghouse has placed conditional purchase orders for safety-related modules with four Polish companies, a week after being commissioned to begin ordering long-lead items for the first unit of Poland's planned first nuclear power plant.

articles.title: WANO stresses importance of collaboration for nuclear growth
articles.summary: "As nuclear energy expands globally, success will depend on our ability to learn faster, collaborate more deeply and translate insight into action," said World Association of Nuclear Operators CEO Naoki Chigusa.

articles.title: Second part of construction permit application submitted for SMRs at Palisades
articles.summary: Holtec has submitted the Preliminary Safety Analysis Report to the US Nuclear Regulatory Commission for two small modular reactor units at the Palisades Energy Center in Michigan, completing the second phase of the Construction Permit Application process.

articles.title: Last Energy's Texas micro-modular reactor clears safety analysis
articles.summary: The Department of Energy's approval of the Documented Safety Analysis clears Last Energy's planned pilot reactor at Texas A&M-RELLIS to move into the readiness review, the final step before authorisation for criticality and reactor operations.

articles.title: Latest Terrestrial Energy topical report submission could lead to faster deployment
articles.summary: Approval of the Thermal and Electric Facility Topical Report submitted by the company to US regulators would mean that part of the Integrated Molten Salt Reactor plant would be classed as a conventional industrial, rather than nuclear, project, allowing it to be built and operated ahead of nuclear licensing.
